data.title: Proteomic Profiling of Potential E6AP Substrates via Ubiquitin-based Photo-Crosslinking Assisted Affinity Enrichment
data.projectDescription: E6AP/UBE3A, the founding member of HECT-type (Homologous to E6AP C-terminus) E3 ligases, is implicated in human papillomaviruses (HPV)-mediated cervical cancer and neurodevelopmental disorders like Angelman and Dup15q syndromes. To elucidate the function of E3 ligases, knowledge about their substrates is crucial. Their identification, however, is challenging due to complex cross-reactivities between E2, E3 and their substrates. To address this, we developed a novel ubiquitin-based photo labeling approach for HECT-type ligases. Our method modifies ubiquitin with a diazirine moiety and attaches it to E6AP's active site using the ubiquitination cascade and a Cys to Lys mutation. The resulting E6AP-Ub conjugate enables substrate trapping via photoaffinity labeling and proteomic profiling. We validated this approach through literature comparison and identified Ub C-terminal hydrolase 7 (Uchl5/Uch37) as a new, proteasome-independent ubiquitination target of E6AP. This method expands the toolbox for substrate identification, potentially providing deeper insights into E6AP-related cellular processes and other HECT-type E3 ligases.
data.sampleProcessingProtocol: For the affinity enrichment assay 200 pmol of each bait (tS-E6AP C820K-Ub 3C-DEA, tS-E6AP C820K and His-Ub-tS 3C-DEA, buffer for empty bead control) were immobilized on 10 µL of StrepTactin XT beads (IBA Lifescience) by incubation with overhead rotation at 4°C for 4 h. Following a wash with cell lysis buffer (25 mM Tris, 50 mM NaCl, pH=7.5, 1 mM DTT, 0.1 % NP-40, Roche cOmplete Ultra Protease Inhibitor cocktail) the beads were transferred to a low retention 96 well plate (Greiner Bio) and 1 mg of HEK293T lysate was added. The mixtures were incubated overnight at 10°C with shaking at 600 rpm. The E6AP C820K and empty beads samples were transferred to Mobicol Spin columns (MoBiTec Molecular Biotechnology) covered in aluminum foil and placed on ice with the 96 well plate. Samples were irradiated in a 365 nm UV chamber (Bio-Link 365, Vilber Lourmat) with a dosage of2.4 J/cm2. After photocrosslinking the remaining samples were transferred to Mobicol Spin columns as well and the flow through was collected. The samples were washed five times with 200 µL Wash buffer (100 mM Tris, 150 mM NaCl, 0.5 M urea, 1 mM EDTA, pH = 8) and once reconditioned to Wash buffer without urea. Subsequent elution was achieved through incubation at 25 °C for 15 minutes twice with 100 µL Elution Buffer (100 mM Tris, 150 mM NaCl, 50 mM Biotin, 1 mM EDTA, pH = 8) and once with 50 µL Elution buffer and further incubation with the collected 250 µL. Samples (FT, Wash 5, Elution, beads) were analyzed on 12.5 % SDS-PA gels. The remaining sample was lyophilized and stored at -20 C until further processing. Prior to LC-MS/MS analysis proteins were proteolyzed by trypsin (Promega) following the in-gel digestion protocol from Shevchenko et al.[3] The experiment was conducted in biological triplicate.Prior to mass spectrometric analysis, all samples were desalted and concentrated by PierceTM C18 Spin Tips (Thermo Scientific).  All digested samples were analyzed by reversed phase liquid chromatography nanospray tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) using a Q Exactive HF Hybrid Quadrupole-Orbitrap mass spectrometer (Thermo Scientific), coupled to an Easy-nLC 1200 (Thermo Scientific). The dimensions of the reversed-phase LC column were 2 μm, 100 Å pore size C18 resin in a 50 μm i.d. × 15 cm long piece of fused silica capillary (Acclaim PepMapTM RSLC, Thermo Scientific). After sample injection, the column was washed for 4 min with 94% mobile phase A (0.1% formic acid) and 6% mobile phase B (0.1% formic acid in acetonitrile/water (80:20, v/v)), and peptides were eluted using a linear gradient of 6% mobile phase B to 40% mobile phase B in 62 min, followed by 1 min to 100% B, and a washing step with 100% B in an additional 8 min. The Q Exactive HF mass spectrometer was operated in a data dependent Top20 mode with dynamic exclusion set to 30 sec. Full MS scan spectra were acquired at a resolution 120,000 (at m/z 200), scan range 350-1500 m/z with an automatic gain control target value of 3e6 and a maximum injection time of 60 ms. Most intense precursor ions with charge states of 2-5 reaching a minimum automatic gain control target value of 1e3 were selected for MS/MS experiments. Normalized collision energy was set to 28%. MS/MS spectra were collected at a resolution of 15,000 (at m/z 200), an automatic gain control target value of 1e5 and 50 ms maximum injection time.
data.dataProcessingProtocol: Raw files were analyzed using the MaxQuant software (version 2.1.4.0)[4] with the Andromeda search engine and the default settings and label-free quantification (LFQ, minimum ratio count 2) enabled. Proteins were identified using a human reference proteome downloaded from the UniProt database (download date: 04/02/2019, https://www.uniprot.org/proteomes/) and an integrated database of common contaminants. Further processing was performed with the Perseus software (version 2.0.11.0).[5] Proteins identified in the initial analysis were filtered to exclude those identified only by site, reverse hits, and potential contaminants. The LFQ values were transformed using the Log2 function, and the proteins were filtered to be quantified in at least 70% of all replicates for a given condition (three biological replicates, two technical replicates). Missing values were imputed from a normal distribution (width = 0.3, shift = 1.8) separately for each column, and technical duplicates were averaged to avoid any falsification in subsequent statistical analysis. The enriched proteins were identified through a one-way ANOVA multiple-sample test (S0 = 1, FDR = 0.05). The results of the ANOVA were subjected to a post hoc Tukey test (FDR = 0.05), and the matrix was filtered for significant pairs (E6AP-Ub > controls). Additionally, Ub samples that were enriched over E6AP-Ub were removed. Subsequently, the results were subjected to z-scoring, after which a hierarchal cluster was constructed based on their Euclidean distance.
